```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = FALSE,
  comment = ""
)
library(cucumber)

# testthat forces ASCII "v"/"x" step symbols while it captures reporter output,
# so pin cli to ASCII everywhere for a consistent look (this also matches the
# package's own test snapshots). Colour is dropped automatically because cli
# detects no ANSI support in a non-interactive knit.
options(cli.unicode = FALSE)

# Durations change on every run, so show fixed ones to keep README.md stable.
for (hook in c("output", "error")) {
  local({
    default <- knitr::knit_hooks$get(hook)
    knitr::knit_hooks$set(setNames(list(function(x, options) {
      default(gsub("\\d+m\\d{2}\\.\\d{3}s", "0m00.100s", x), options)
    }), hook))
  })
}

# Reporter output below is produced by running shipped examples, so it can
# never drift from the implementation.
pass_dir <- "inst/examples/with_testthat_success"
fail_dir <- "inst/examples/with_testthat_failure"
feature_file <- "tests/acceptance/addition.feature"
steps_file <- "tests/acceptance/setup-steps-addition.R"

# Helper: fence a file's contents so the displayed example is the exact same
# source that is executed further down.
embed <- function(path, lang) {
  cat(sprintf("```%s\n", lang))
  cat(readLines(path), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n```\n")
}
```

Write specifications in plain-language [Gherkin](https://cucumber.io/docs/gherkin/reference/), run them from R as testthat tests, and read the results in the console or in Cucumber's own HTML report. An R implementation of the [Cucumber](https://cucumber.io/) testing framework.

## Installation

```r
install.packages("cucumber")
```

## Where to start

- **New to cucumber?** [Get started](https://jakubsob.github.io/cucumber/articles/get-started.html): write and run your first feature.
- **New to BDD?** Read [Behavior-Driven Development](https://jakubsob.github.io/cucumber/articles/bdd.html).
- **Know testthat?** See [cucumber and testthat](https://jakubsob.github.io/cucumber/articles/testthat.html).
- **Looking something up?** Open the [function reference](https://jakubsob.github.io/cucumber/reference/) or the [Gherkin reference](https://jakubsob.github.io/cucumber/articles/reference-gherkin.html).

## Run your first feature

A feature file describes behavior in Gherkin

```{r feature, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
embed(file.path(pass_dir, feature_file), "gherkin")
```

and step definitions run each step in R

```{r steps, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
embed(file.path(pass_dir, steps_file), "r")
```

Each Feature is a testthat context and each Scenario a `testthat::test_that()` case, so you get feedback on each Scenario separately. Run them with `cucumber::test()`:

```{r run-pass}
withr::with_dir(pass_dir, {
  cucumber::test(filter = "addition")
})
```

When a step fails, the reporter shows which step broke and why, and where its definition is. [Get started](https://jakubsob.github.io/cucumber/articles/get-started.html) walks through a failure, the other console reporters and where to put the files.

## Reports

Write the official Cucumber HTML report of a run with `CucumberHtmlReporter`, and its JUnit XML report with `CucumberJunitReporter`. Steps and hooks attach screenshots and logs to it, like those of a failing [shinytest2](https://rstudio.github.io/shinytest2/) scenario: see the [Reports article](https://jakubsob.github.io/cucumber/articles/reporting.html) and [its report](https://jakubsob.github.io/cucumber/shinytest2-report.html).

## Scenarios as documentation

Feature files already say how your package behaves, so let them document it. Tag the scenarios that illustrate a function with `@rd`

```{r rd-feature, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
rd_feature <- c(
  "Feature: Basket",
  "  A basket holds the items a customer wants to buy.",
  "",
  "  @rd",
  "  Scenario: Add an item",
  "    Given an empty basket",
  "    When I add 1 item",
  "    Then the basket has 1 item",
  "",
  "  Scenario: Remove an item from an empty basket",
  "    Given an empty basket",
  "    When I remove 1 item",
  "    Then the basket is empty"
)
rd_roxygen <- c(
  "#' Add items to a basket",
  "#' @eval cucumber::features_rd(features = \"basket.feature\")",
  "#' @export",
  "add <- function(basket, n) basket + n"
)
cat("```gherkin", rd_feature, "```", sep = "\n")
```

and put them in its help page with `features_rd()`:

```{r rd-roxygen, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("```r", rd_roxygen, "```", sep = "\n")
```

`devtools::document()` adds a Behavior section to `?add` with the feature's description and the tagged scenarios:

```{r rd-help, echo = FALSE}
withr::with_tempdir({
  dir.create("tests/acceptance", recursive = TRUE)
  writeLines(rd_feature, "tests/acceptance/basket.feature")
  rd <- roxygen2::roc_proc_text(roxygen2::rd_roclet(), paste(rd_roxygen, collapse = "\n"))
  rd_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".Rd")
  writeLines(format(rd[["add.Rd"]]), rd_file)
  help <- capture.output(tools::Rd2txt(rd_file, options = list(underline_titles = FALSE)))
  #section <- paste0(getOption("cucumber.rd_section"), ":")
  #cat(help[which(help == section):length(help)], sep = "\n")
  cat(help, sep = "\n")
})
```

The help pages of this package are written this way, see [`?hook`](https://jakubsob.github.io/cucumber/reference/hook.html) or [`?test`](https://jakubsob.github.io/cucumber/reference/test.html): the scenarios that test cucumber explain it, and stay true because they run.

How steps are matched, and the parameter types you can use, are in [How it works](https://jakubsob.github.io/cucumber/articles/how-it-works.html).
